Contributing to bdhs

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for helping improve bdhs. Bug reports, questions, ideas and pull requests are all welcome.

Never share DHS microdata

The DHS Program does not allow respondent-level data to be redistributed. Please do not attach .dta, .sav, .zip or other data files, or paste rows of microdata, into issues or pull requests. To show a problem, use synthetic data from bdhs_simulate() or bdhs_synthesize(), or describe the file (survey, recode, file name) and the variables involved.

Reporting a bug

Open an issue at https://github.com/armanhossen-am/bdhs/issues with:

  • what you ran, ideally as a small reproducible example (the reprex package helps);
  • what you expected and what happened instead, including the full error message;
  • the output of sessionInfo() and packageVersion("bdhs").

If an estimate does not match the official DHS value, give the indicator, survey round and both numbers.

Asking for help or suggesting a feature

Open an issue and describe what you are trying to do. The tutorials at https://armanhossen-am.github.io/bdhs/ cover most tasks. You can also email the maintainer, Arman Hossen, at hossena@miamioh.edu.

Contributing code

  1. Fork the repository and create a branch for your change.
  2. Follow the style of the existing code and document new functions with roxygen2 comments.
  3. Add tests with testthat. Tests must run on synthetic data, not on real microdata.
  4. Run devtools::document() and devtools::check() and make sure there are no errors or warnings.
  5. Open a pull request that explains what the change does and why.

DEVELOPMENT.md in the repository describes how the package is organised and the rules it follows.

Code of conduct

Please be respectful and constructive. Harassment or personal attacks are not accepted in issues, pull requests or any other project space.
